sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: You spent Days 1–7 inside Pydantic AI. Days 8 and 9 introduced LangChain (linear chains) and LangGraph (stateful graphs). Today we bring it home: two productivity agents in Pydantic AI that show why this framework is often the best default — type-safe inputs and outputs, decorators for tools and validators, and retry-on-validation-failure for free. You will build a Doc Q&A agent with typed answers and citations, and an Action Item Extractor that rejects malformed output and asks the model to fix itself.

sections.title: Quick Refresher on Key Pydantic AI APIs
sections.body:
The cheat sheet, since you have seen these for seven days:

- **`Agent(model, system_prompt=..., result_type=...)`** — constructs an agent. `result_type` defaults to `str`; set it to a Pydantic model for structured output.
- **`agent.run_sync(user_prompt, deps=...)`** — synchronous one-shot call. Use `await agent.run(...)` for async or `agent.iter()` for streaming.
- **`@agent.system_prompt`** — define a system prompt as a function. Can take `ctx` and is called at runtime. Use this for dynamic context.
- **`@agent.tool` / `@agent.tool_plain`** — register a tool. `@agent.tool` gets a `RunContext`; `@agent.tool_plain` does not.
- **`@agent.result_validator`** — runs after the model produces output, before it is returned. Raise `ModelRetry` to ask the model to retry.
- **`RunContext[Deps]`** — first parameter of tools and dynamic prompts. Gives access to `deps`, `usage`, and `retry` count.

If any feel fuzzy, flip back to the relevant Day 1–7 file.

```bash
pip install pydantic-ai pydantic python-dotenv rich
```

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
- **Forgetting to register the validator as a decorator.** Defining `def reject_empty_owners(...)` without `@extractor.result_validator` does nothing. Always decorate.
- **Raising `ValueError` instead of `ModelRetry`.** A `ValueError` in a result validator propagates as an unhandled exception. Use `ModelRetry` to ask the model to retry; reserve `ValueError` for hard failures.
- **`result_type=list[Model]` vs `result_type=WrapperModel`.** Bare lists work in Pydantic AI 0.0.30+, but older versions prefer a wrapper. If you see "cannot determine result type" errors, switch.
- **Validators that are too strict.** If your validator rejects 80% of attempts, the model exhausts retries and fails with `UsageLimitExceeded`. Loosen the validator or improve the prompt — don't just bump `retries=10`.
- **Dynamic system prompts must be sync by default.** `@agent.system_prompt` on a `def` works. For `async def`, use `@agent.system_prompt(dynamic=True)` and run async. Mismatching raises a confusing `RuntimeError`.
- **Mutating the result inside a validator.** Prefer to return a new object. Forgetting the return statement silently returns `None`, which breaks the agent.
